Modelling meals: the simulated protein term and the estimator built on it

Phases B2 and B3 of docs/plans/08-modelling-meals.md. What was built, what it was checked against, what the checks said, and what is still not established. This is a build report: unlike 05-fitting-ba-and-isf.html it keeps the defects found on the way, because a scenario library is a measuring instrument and how it was found to be wrong is part of what says whether to trust it now.

Why these phases exist

Phase 5 established that the fasting formulation cannot determine ISF from this record. The exclusion window moves the answer from 7.6 to 67.6, the estimate never plateaus, and every route to removing the meal bias runs through discarding the data that carries the meal. The response is to model meals rather than exclude them:

dbg_per_h(t)  =  BA(h)  −  ISF × IA(t)  +  CSF_c × CA_c(t)  +  CSF_p × CA_p(t)  +  e(t)

fitted on every row rather than on the 13% a 4 h / 8 h filter allows. B2 gives the simulator a protein term so there is a truth to check that against; B3 builds the estimator and measures what it can and cannot recover.

B2 — the simulator's protein term

Before this, protein was absorbed on the carbohydrate path at its entered grams with the carbohydrate sensitivity. Protein is entered at half its weight, so that is a protein-to-carbohydrate equivalence of exactly 0.50 — the owner's dosing convention, asserted as physiology. His own whey-isolate measurements put it nearer 0.20. It is now a parameter.

parametermeaningdefault
csf_ratioCSF_p / CSF_c, per real gram0.50
delay_minminutes before any protein appears10
absorption_multipliertrue duration ÷ the entered time1.00
kappacarbohydrate suppresses how much protein converts0
deltacarbohydrate delays protein's onset0
taucarbohydrate stretches protein's duration0
rhoprotein slows carbohydrate down0

The defaults reproduce the old simulator exactly

Not approximately: a 90-day scenario built before the change and one built after agree on all 25,790 glucose readings, with identical entries, boluses and temp basals. That is what lets the 61 scenarios already on disk stay valid instead of being regenerated, and it is pinned by a test rather than trusted. Scenarios written before the block existed are scored by defaulting it, which is not a guess — those runs were the defaults.

Why protein_sensitivity had to be designed three times

This is the most useful thing B2 learned, and it is a constraint on what the record can ever say.

First attempt — sweep the ratio, hold the convention. The loop doses insulin for protein glucose that never arrives, and on a pure integrator with no glucose-dependent disposal that accumulates without bound. Measured: 54.5% time in range at ratio 0.30, 35.3% at 0.20, 17.2% at 0.10, with 30–73% of readings pinned at the clamp. A clamped series cannot move, so a fit on it measures the clamp. Scaling the protein bolus down proportionally took ratio 0.10 from 0.0% to 17.2% and no further — the deficit is far larger than the bolus — and the oracle controller was worse.

Second attempt — move the convention with the truth. Control is then perfect and the sweep measures nothing. The fit sees r/(2c), so a convention that tracks the sensitivity returns CSF_c/2 at every level. A record identifies the product — true glucose per entered gram — and not the sensitivity and the convention separately. That is not a limitation of this estimator; it is what the data contains.

Third and current — move both, keeping the mismatch controllable. Two blocks at different conventions, each spanning the same mismatch, reach true ratios from 0.15 to 0.80 where a fixed convention stops at 0.35. The owner's measured 0.20 is inside. The blocks look nearly identical to the fit and differ in physiology, which is what makes running both worth the scenarios.

One consequence for B5: the fit's output is directly the number the entry convention needs, and is not the absolute protein sensitivity. Any statement about the latter has to come from the fasted tests.

Control quality is validated, and it is not a formality

Every level is checked for at least 25% of readings in 60–140 mg/dL and at most 10% at the plausibility clamp. Four scenarios failed that check during development and were redesigned rather than fitted.

B3 — the estimator

The parameters split cleanly, and the split is the whole design.

kindparametershow they are solved
linear24 × BA(h), ISF, CSF_c, CSF_p — 27 in allleast squares, exactly, in about 3 ms
non-lineartwo delays, two durations, kappa, delta, tau, rhosearched over: they change a regressor's shape rather than scaling it

Eliminating the linear block analytically and minimising over the rest is variable projection (Golub & Pereyra, 1973). Because the inner solve is exact, the reduced objective is the profile likelihood under Gaussian errors — so the surfaces below are profile likelihoods, and their curvature is the uncertainty rather than a diagnostic bolted on afterwards.

The outer loop is a grid, then a golden-section polish from the grid minimum. A gradient method is the usual partner for variable projection and is the wrong choice here: Loop's absorption curve is piecewise linear, so the objective is kinked and its gradient jumps at the breakpoints. The grid also produces the surfaces as a by-product, which an optimiser would make extra work, and the whole search costs about 18 seconds per scenario.

Interaction channels are added one at a time, in the order kappa → delta → tau → rho, and each is kept only if it beats its own null — an extra parameter always fits the training data at least as well, so improving the fit is not on its own a reason to carry one.

Results

Recovery across the library

An earlier draft of this report claimed CSF_p was much the hardest of the three to pin, on the strength of a synthetic test where it ranged 0.48 to 1.36 across seeds. The library says otherwise — the three spreads are 0.168, 0.171 and 0.179 — and the disagreement turned out to be about the test, not the parameter.

The BA(h) smoothness penalty had to be abandoned

Plan 08's decision 3 was to keep plan 07's penalty on the hourly profile. That is now reversed, on measurement.

Decision 1: what should the search optimise?

Selection has to be on held-out predictive error, because that is the only objective the real record offers. Plan 07 found that objective diverging from parameter recovery, so the same search was run twice on every scenario — once on held-out error, once against declared truth — and both were compared to the true value.

Error is the distance from the held-out choice to the truth, as a share of the swept range; 0.5 is what guessing produces. Flatness is the share of the swept range scoring within 1% of the minimum — near 1 means the data did not choose.

what was wronghow it showedconsequence had it stood

carb_delay had no truth knob at allthe search grid included it and nothing in the library could move ita parameter fitted on the record with no way to check it

What is established, and what is not

Established. The estimator recovers ISF, CSF_c and CSF_p across the library; it reduces exactly to the Phase 5 fit when the meal terms are absent, so the comparison B5 rests on is like-for-like; held-out prediction is a sound objective for choosing the shape; and the BA(h) penalty must be off when the meal terms are present.

Not established. delta and tau are not identifiable by any objective tried, even in the families built to isolate them — both sit where guessing sits. rho is marginal and kappa weak with a flat surface, which means plan 08's prediction 4 is heading for a qualified answer rather than a clean one. Nothing here has touched the real record: every number on this page is simulated, and B5 is where that changes.

Deferred. Fat is not recorded and its attenuating effect on protein cannot be fitted; the protein_6h versus protein_8h contrast that was the only read on it has been dropped by the decision to fit one pooled protein class. Prediction 6 is untestable until a four-class A/B runs.
